account:
Something unusual seems to be being prepared for eighteen hundred in the town hall. The innkeeper described a hospitality committee involving the innkeeper, builder and freight, said bread was reserved, and promised explanations at eighteen. Neighbour reported 201 fresh loaves in the hall, baked yesterday. That is a substantial provision for a gathering. Freight checked the hall schedule with secretary, and secretary confirmed that I would be escorted inside precisely at eighteen, not earlier. I agreed not to arrive early, but I still have not been told the purpose or who the guests are.

Townspeople repeatedly mention a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. One account named baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour as having been there, and said builder carried a sack of bread at the bakery and square_north_1. I have not witnessed any actual bridge or port change, and these repeated reports may all come from the same rumour. The bread movements seem consistent with preparations for the committee's gathering, but that connection is not established.

My best guess is that this is a planned communal meal or surprise occasion whose purpose is deliberately being kept from me until tonight. I cannot yet tell whether it celebrates anything, concerns town infrastructure, or is simply hospitality. Nothing I have personally observed establishes wrongdoing.

Ordinary official business has meanwhile been strangely thin: no council correspondence or account ledgers have been supplied, and today's scheduled mill inspection had no identifiable host or reserves report. Secretary says the inspection was already on my schedule and does not know who arranged it. These may be ordinary organisational failures rather than part of the preparations. I attended the mill at ten and have now looked inside the bakery without finding the baker. I intend to keep my remaining appointments, especially the eighteen-hundred hall meeting, while seeking firsthand explanations rather than treating gossip as fact.
